properties.name: Eastern Queens to Midtown Manhattan
properties.destination: Midtown East (Lexington Av / 53rd St, Congestion Zone)
properties.difficulty: Walking access and transfer connections consume 17.7 minutes (31.8% of the trip). The bus ride itself is only 6.9 minutes.
properties.evidence: Queens residents hold 343,646 payroll jobs in Manhattan (LODES 2023); 36,439 daily car trips enter Manhattan from Queens boroughwide (CMS 2024).
properties.car_evidence: Queens has a 34.8% boroughwide car-driver mode share (CMS 2024); Fresh Meadows sits beyond walking distance of any subway station.
properties.proposed_response: Automated Bus Lane Enforcement (ABLE) and Transit Signal Priority (TSP) on arterial feeder corridors (Union Tpke / Utopia Pkwy), combined with weather-protected bus-subway intermodal transfer bays at 169th St / Kew Gardens.
properties.why_helps: Slightly reduces feeder delay and protects transfer connections, making the 28.5-minute express subway leg more attractive; however, pedestrian first-mile access remains a fundamental physical constraint.
properties.missing_evidence: Neighbourhood-specific peak car trips specifically entering the Manhattan CBD; exact Q30 headway regularity and speed data; ridership elasticity to feeder restructuring.

properties.name: East Bronx to Midtown Manhattan
properties.destination: Midtown East (Grand Central-42nd St, Congestion Zone)
properties.difficulty: Overall trip exceeds 71 minutes; the feeder bus leg is 16.0 minutes in mixed traffic, followed by a long 42.5-minute subway express run.
properties.evidence: Bronx residents hold 206,562 payroll jobs in Manhattan (LODES 2023); Bronx generates 102,489 daily car-driver trips into Manhattan (25.58% mode share, CMS 2024).
properties.car_evidence: Bronx car-driver share to Manhattan is 25.58% (highest of all boroughs); Throggs Neck is a peninsular community with immediate access to the Throgs Neck Bridge, Bruckner, and Cross Bronx Expressways.
properties.proposed_response: Bus lane priority, queue-bypass lanes, and Transit Signal Priority on feeder approaches to the #6 train along Westchester Ave / Crosby Ave; station accessibility upgrades at Buhre Ave.
properties.why_helps: Reduces feeder bus delay and headway variability connecting to the #6 train, lowering the transit time penalty against driving via the Bruckner Expressway for commuters destined for Midtown East.
properties.missing_evidence: Specific Bx8 bottleneck locations; local auto ownership rates in Throggs Neck; commuter willingness to switch modes given a 65-to-70-minute transit baseline.

properties.name: Southeast Queens to Lower Manhattan
properties.difficulty: Commuter rail running time is rapid (27.0 min for 14 miles), but transferring to the subway requires an 8.5-minute outdoor walk between Nostrand Ave stations, with separate fares.
properties.evidence: Queens residents hold 343,646 payroll jobs in Manhattan; Lower Manhattan hosts major municipal, legal, and financial employment centers.
properties.car_evidence: Southeast Queens has high automobile ownership; boroughwide Queens driving share is 34.8% (CMS 2024); direct subway access is absent.
properties.proposed_response: Direct enclosed or weather-protected intermodal transfer concourse between LIRR Nostrand Ave and A/C subway stations; full OMNY cross-honoring / fare-free rail-to-subway transfer integration.
properties.why_helps: Eliminates physical transfer friction and financial double-payment, unlocking fast commuter rail capacity for outer Queens commuters without requiring highway driving on the Belt Parkway.
properties.missing_evidence: Capital engineering feasibility and cost of a Nostrand Ave intermodal connection; operating revenue impact of full LIRR-subway fare integration; daily passenger transfer counts at Nostrand Ave.

properties.name: Union Turnpike Feeder Bus Priority & Kew Gardens Hub
properties.origin: Eastern Queens (Springfield Blvd to Kew Gardens)
properties.destination: Grand Central / Midtown East (via E/F Express Subway)
properties.difficulty: Feeder bus run times along arterial reach 21 to 41 minutes; transfer friction at Kew Gardens interchange adds 8 minutes.
properties.evidence: Stage 5 multimodal simulation across 6 origins demonstrates 6.2 to 12.5 minutes savings (11.9% to 15.2% reduction; average 8.7 min / 13.5%).
properties.car_evidence: 7 matched census tracts host 2,649 congestion-zone jobs and high drive-alone rates (30% to 60%).
properties.proposed_response: Peak bus lanes, Transit Signal Priority (TSP), off-board OMNY payment, and sheltered intermodal transfer bays.
properties.why_helps: Tackles both feeder in-vehicle delay and transfer dwell, connecting passengers to fast E/F subway trunk.
properties.missing_evidence: Tract-level driver destination shares into tolled core; on-street TSP conflict points with crosstown traffic.
